verses.commentary: When Ephraim spoke, people trembled. Former power. He was exalted in Israel. Leadership position. But he became guilty of Baal worship and died. The turning point. Spiritual death through idolatry.

Now they sin more and more. Progression in evil. They make idols from their silver. Wealth funds false worship. Cleverly fashioned images. Artistic skill in service of folly. They offer human sacrifices! They kiss calf-idols! The shocking practices stated.

They will be like morning mist. Brief appearance, quick vanishing. Like early dew that disappears. The recurring image for fleeting repentance and fleeting existence. Like chaff from the threshing floor. Blown away. Like smoke from a window. Dispersing into nothing.
I have been the Lord your God ever since Egypt. Ancient relationship. You shall acknowledge no God but me. First commandment. No Savior except me. Exclusive salvation. The foundation of covenant.
I cared for you in the wilderness. Desert provision. In the land of burning heat. Hostile environment survived by grace. God's historical faithfulness.
When I fed them, they were satisfied. Provision received. When they were satisfied, they became proud. Prosperity produced arrogance. Then they forgot me. The pattern. Blessing leads to amnesia.
So I will be like a lion to them. God as predator. Like a leopard I will lurk by the path. Waiting in ambush. The shepherd becomes the hunter.

Like a bear robbed of her cubs. Fierce maternal rage. I will attack them and rip them open. Violent imagery. Like a lion I will devour them. Complete destruction. A wild animal will tear them apart. Total devastation.
You are destroyed, Israel, because you are against me. The diagnosis. Against your helper. They oppose their only aid. Self-destruction through opposition to God.

Where is your king, that he may save you? Challenge. Where are your rulers in all your towns? The ones they trusted. Of whom you said: Give me a king and princes. Their own request (1 Samuel 8). The monarchy they demanded.
In my anger I gave you a king. God granted their request as judgment. In my wrath I took him away. The king given becomes the king removed. The monarchy brackets their history.
The guilt of Ephraim is stored up. Accumulating record. His sins are kept on record. Nothing forgotten. The account continues.

Pains as of a woman in childbirth come to him. Labor metaphor. But he is a child without wisdom. Unable to be born properly. When the time arrives, he doesn't have the sense to come out of the womb. Stuck, foolish, unable to emerge into new life.

I will deliver this people from the power of the grave. Promise of redemption. I will redeem them from death. Resurrection hope. Where, O death, are your plagues? Where, O grave, is your destruction? Paul quotes this in 1 Corinthians 15:55 for resurrection victory. I will have no compassion. Or: compassion will be hidden from my eyes. The verse holds both judgment and hope.

Even though he thrives among his brothers. Temporary prosperity. An east wind from the Lord will come. The sirocco, divine weapon. Blowing in from the desert. Drying, destroying. His spring will fail, his well dry up. Water sources exhausted. His storehouse plundered. Accumulated wealth lost.

The people of Samaria must bear their guilt. Responsibility assigned. Because they have rebelled against their God. The reason clear. They will fall by the sword. Military defeat. Their little ones dashed to the ground. War's horror. Their pregnant women ripped open. Atrocity. The chapter ends in darkness before the final chapter's dawn.
